An Inviting Dining Experience
Jun 2026 • Solo
First, I got the sea bass & passion fruit tiradito. The fish was fresh, and the slices were evenly cut. The foamy sauce was a creative touch, and I loved how it balanced sour, spicy, sweet, and salty flavors. The passion fruit's acidity was the most prominent, but the other flavors still came through. My only issue was the crispy corn kernels. With every bite, I tried to justify the need to add the kernels, but I couldn't. They didn't add any noticeable corn flavor, and I found their hard texture distracting against the delicate fish and silky sauce. I also would have preferred a bit more sea bass visible on the plating, though that's just a personal preference.
Next were the beef and chicken empanadas. I had high expectations since I love empanadas, but they didn't quite deliver. The beef empanada had a crispy, golden crust and was filled with tender, well-seasoned beef. However, the filling tended to spill out after every bite.
The chicken empanada was the weaker of the two. Its filling didn't feel harmonious or satisfying. It seemed like an ingredient was either missing or out of place. It wasn't bland, but it lacked the depth I was hoping for. I was also expecting the same crispy exterior as the beef empanada, but the chicken version fell short in that regard. Both empanadas were served hot, which I appreciated.
Lastly, I had the mushroom quesadilla, which ended up being my favorite dish. The tortilla was nicely toasted and crispy, while the filling was soft, savory, and packed with earthy mushroom flavor. As a truffle lover, I really enjoyed the truffle notes throughout the dish. I was only disappointed by the lack of melted cheese, as I expected it to play a bigger role. 
I also want to mention that all the accompaniments, including the chimichurri, pico de gallo, and truffle aioli, were house-made rather than store-bought, and they elevated every dish they accompanied. Beyond the food, I appreciated how well-prepared each plate was, how organized and attentive the staff were, and the warm, welcoming atmosphere that tied the whole experience together.

A Masterclass in How Not to Run a Restaurant
Jan 2026 • Business
I wanted to give this place a chance. I really did. But their complete incompetence at the most basic function of a restaurant, taking reservations, left me no choice but to warn everyone I know.

Let me paint the picture: I filled out their online reservation form. Nothing. Silence. So I filled it out again. Still nothing. Maybe the system was broken? I called. Once. Twice. Three times. Four times. Five times. Six times. Seven times. Each time, the phone rang into the void. No voicemail. No callback. Just dead air.

This isn't a minor inconvenience; this is a restaurant that apparently doesn't want customers. They've made it functionally impossible to give them money. How do you run an establishment in 2026 and not answer your phone or respond to reservation requests? It's not ambitious. It's not a style choice. It's negligence.

The only explanation is that this restaurant is staffed by people who either don't care or don't understand the fundamentals of hospitality. If they can't manage the front door, what does the kitchen look like?

Don't waste your time, energy, or optimism. There are dozens of restaurants in this city run by people who actually want your business. Go to any of them instead.
